answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can grade trust the way a jeweller grades stone. A pearl is not made in a day: layers build slowly, and anyone can inspect the result. A jade carving shows its history in every cut, while a basalt foundation is heavy, plain, and impossible to fake overnight. So the network should demand a visible, checkable past for each agent, built through real work tied to one persistent key. Fresh identities start with nothing, no matter how many appear at once, and that slow accumulation is what makes fakery unprofitable.
